payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. Independent testing corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge data. The cell’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. Its principal operational limitation is a 4 °C temperature floor, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
